critical_code_review_comments: server.py lookup_invitation returns 404 (not 410) when a stale invitation has status='expired' (post-reissue), because the query short-circuits before invite_expired() check. Spec says '/join/{token} lookup returns 410 for expired'. Currently only invitations that are still status='pending' AND past 14d return 410; post-reissue tokens return 404 with 'no longer valid'. Frontend/UX-wise this is OK, but if the spec strictly requires 410 for any expired token (including reissued/status='expired'), consider handling status=='expired' before the pending guard.
MatterNotes.jsx loads notes on every panel mount and after every save (load() call). Fine at current volume; consider optimistic update to avoid extra GET.
FamilyMatters.jsx reissue handler uses toast for both success/error and reload; no loading spinner on the button during the call. Minor UX polish.

rca of the issue: No functional issues. Only observation: lookup endpoint returns 404 instead of 410 for tokens whose parent invitation was moved to status='expired' by a prior reissue. This is because line 1098 rejects any non-pending invitation with 404 before line 1100's date-based 410 check runs. Not affecting current UX (frontend only surfaces reissue button, never asks user to re-visit the old link), but flag if the acceptance criterion strictly requires 410 for stale reissued tokens.
